category_title: Non-verbal male students with classic autism who struggle with functional communication and use tactile tracing for letter recognition
student_description: This student is a 9-11 year old male with classic autism who struggles with natural speech and traditional communication devices like the Springboard Lite. He requires alternative, highly engaging communication methods, specifically responding well to iPad-based interventions that offer tactile tracing, picture-based communication, and instant auditory or text-based rewards.

criteria.rationale: Immediate auditory and text-based rewards are necessary to motivate this student to continue working and engaging with the material.
criteria.check: The tutor provides or explicitly cues an immediate auditory or text-based reward (e.g., a sound of praise or on-screen text) in response to the student's engagement.

criteria.criterion_name: Elimination of Verbal and Legacy Device Demands
criteria.rationale: Because the student cannot functionally use natural speech or the Springboard Lite device, demanding these will cause immediate disengagement.
criteria.check: The tutor provides an alternative way to communicate (e.g., iPad interaction) and explicitly avoids demanding natural speech or the use of the Springboard Lite device.
